message: I need a management system for my pharmacy business. We are growing and the current way of managing things is becoming difficult.
Who are the different users or roles that will use this system?

We’ll have the usual pharmacy crew: pharmacists, techs, cashiers, managers and the admin folks who handle the back‑office. Each branch will need those same people on the system, plus whoever’s pulling orders from suppliers or handling reimbursements. No extra fancy roles – just the people who already do the day‑to‑day work.
Do you operate from a single location or multiple locations or branches?
We’re still one store right now, but we’re moving to a handful of branches soon. The system has to work across all of them without adding extra headaches.
How do you currently track your inventory, records, or data, and what problems come up?

We’re still doing most of it on paper and a few old Excel sheets – a pharmacist writes down every batch, a tech scans a barcode into a simple log, and the manager pulls a PDF at the end of the month. It’s slow, easy to mis‑type, and the data never syncs between branches. We keep missing expiry dates, double‑counting stock, and the audit trail is shaky. It’s a compliance risk and a headache when a rush hits. We need a single, real‑time view that tells us exactly what we have, where it’s stored, and who handled it.
Walk me through what happens in your core daily workflow from start to finish.

When the store opens we first run a quick inventory scan of the high‑volume aisles and check the expiry lists against the stock register – that’s the only time we catch a batch that’s gone bad before we get customers in. Then the pharmacists take the prescriptions that come in through the counter or the pharmacy software, verify the patient details, check for any drug interactions or refill eligibility, and hand off the controlled meds to a tech who scans the barcode into the system. The techs do the same for the over‑the‑counter items, then the cashier processes the payment and the pharmacy’s reimbursement forms, all while the manager watches the sales dashboard for any spikes or shortages. At closing we run a quick end‑of‑day reconciliation: the system pulls the day’s sales, counts the remaining stock, flags any discrepancies, and the manager signs off the report so we’re ready to restock the next morning. All of this is done on a single screen so no one has to jump between spreadsheets or paper logs.
How do payments or transactions get handled and reconciled today?

We do the usual cash‑in‑hand and card swipe at the counter. The cashier punches the sale into a simple register that prints a receipt, then we hand the slip to the admin office to file the reimbursement form for insurance or pharmacy benefit managers. At closing the admin pulls the daily sales totals from the register, does a quick count of the remaining stock, and compares it to the sales log. If anything looks off the manager signs off the reconciliation sheet, and we flag the discrepancy to investigate.
What reporting or visibility do you need across the business?

We need real‑time dashboards that show inventory levels, expiry alerts, and stock movement per aisle and per branch. A quick sales trend report by category and by pharmacist, plus a reconciliation report that flags any mismatches between sales, inventory and cash. Also a controlled‑meds audit trail that shows who handled what and when, and a purchase‑order status sheet so we know when suppliers are on time. All of that should be pull‑able in a few clicks, not a spreadsheet grind.
What other tools or systems does this need to work with?
